findings.affected_surface: src/runners/review.js dispatchReview composition; src/runners/review-packet.js byte-identical constraint; plan §1.3, §2, §6
findings.claim: The plan contradicts itself about where the defaults floor is enforced: §1.3 says the builder re-adds defaults even if a caller passes a bare extra list, but §0 documents normalizeDenyList as accepting any array as given (case (f) empty list) and §2 keeps review-packet.js byte-identical, so the builder cannot re-add anything. The floor exists only in the review.js spread, and §6 'impossible by construction' overstates it; an implementer trusting §1.3 could pass only the extra list and silently drop every default.
findings.evidence: §1.3: 'buildReviewPacket (which normalizes; defaults are re-added there even if a caller passed a bare extra list)'. §0: 'normalizeDenyList accepts null (→ the default) or an array of strings ... returns a deduped sorted array' and 'cases (e)/(f)/(g) cover ... the empty list'. §2: 'src/runners/review-packet.js: NONE — byte-identical'. §2.6: 'no code path can produce an effective list missing a default pattern'.
findings.evidence_reference: plan §0 bullet 1; §1.3; §2 review-packet.js bullet; §2.6; §6 Silent narrowing
findings.repair: Strike the 're-added there' sentence and name one floor owner explicitly: review.js dispatchReview composes normalizeDenyList([...DEFAULT_PACKET_DENY_LIST, ...denyExtra]) and no other layer ever passes a bare list. Reword §6 to 'guaranteed by the single composition point, asserted by test'. In review-runner.test.sh add cases that the stub builder receives all eight defaults when denyExtra is [] and when the roster omits the field, and that passing a bare extra list to the real builder without going through dispatchReview is not a supported path (documented, not silently defaulted).

findings.affected_surface: scripts/resolve-review-loop.sh element regex; src/engine/resolve-review-loop.js validator; oracle parity case in hooks/tests/resolve-review-loop.test.sh
findings.claim: The character allowlist [A-Za-z0-9._*/-] is a second grammar owner, not a projection of normalizeDenyList. Per §0 the builder rejects only absolute, dot, dot-dot, empty and other-glob patterns, not spaces, plus signs, at-signs, tildes or non-ASCII, and the plan's own wording introduces the allowlist for shell JSON safety. Since the JS resolver validates by calling normalizeDenyList only, a pattern such as docs/a b/** or docs/x+y/** is accepted by the JS side and refused by the shell, which is exactly the shell/JS drift the parity gate is meant to exclude. The described 'both directions' oracle either fails on such strings or, if the table omits them, passes while drift exists.
findings.evidence: §1.2: 'Character allowlist per element: [A-Za-z0-9._*/-] only (no whitespace, no quotes, no backslash — this is what makes the shell's JSON emission safe)' and 'the JS resolver and the engine validate by calling normalizeDenyList' and 'ONE grammar owner — the builder's normalizeDenyList'. §0: normalizeDenyList 'rejects absolute/./../empty/other-glob patterns' (no character-class restriction listed).
findings.repair: Define the effective element grammar once as (allowlist regex AND normalizeDenyList accepts). Export a single shared constant (for example PACKET_DENY_ELEMENT_RE) from src/engine/resolve-review-loop.js, apply it in the JS resolver and in reviewPacketIdentity before calling normalizeDenyList, and make the shell regex the projection of that constant. Make the oracle predicate the composed one and extend the inline table with space, plus, at-sign, tilde, non-ASCII and comma probes so the shell accept/reject equals the composed JS predicate in both directions. Alternatively verify at base that normalizeDenyList already enforces this character class and cite the exact check; if it does not, the byte-identical builder constraint and the one-owner claim cannot both hold and the plan must pick one.

findings.evidence_reference: plan §2.5; §4.1 mirror gate paragraph; §4 scope-integrity row
findings.repair: Re-check mirror roots at base before sealing. If platforms/codex/plugin/project-config-template/review-loop-config.md exists, add it to §2.5 and to the docs bullet in §2; if the root is not mirrored, correct the pair count to six and state that the template has no mirror. findings.affected_surface: src/engine/autopilot-engine.js both packet call sites; reviewPacketIdentity prepare gate
findings.claim: The specified call-site expression roster.review_packet_deny_extra || [] coerces any falsy non-array value (empty string, 0, false) to the default list silently instead of blocking at prepare time. The plan explicitly contemplates hand-built rosters, so a roster carrying an empty-string field would fall back to defaults without a block, contrary to the malformed-blocks rule.
findings.evidence: §1.3: 'both engine packet call sites pass denyExtra: roster.review_packet_deny_extra || []' and 'the resolver already refused it, but a hand-built roster can carry one; the block happens before any seat is spent'. §4 plumbing row: 'malformed → prepare_review block; absent ⇒ []'.
findings.repair: Treat only undefined and null as absent (nullish coalescing or an explicit hasOwnProperty check) and pass every other value to reviewPacketIdentity so its Array.isArray gate produces the packet deny extra malformed block. Add an autopilot-engine.test.sh case with the roster field set to an empty string and to false, asserting the prepare_review block rather than a default-list packet.

findings.affected_surface: hooks/tests/review-runner.test.sh stub-builder case; JS resolver element-indexed message; shell emission order
findings.claim: Three test mechanics are assumed but not described: how review-runner.test.sh substitutes a stub buildReviewPacket into review.js (no injection seam is mentioned; the builder is a direct import), how the JS resolver produces review_packet_deny_extra[i] with an index when normalizeDenyList validates a whole array, and whether the shell sorts/dedupes the emitted array as the 'valid list echoed sorted/deduped' case expects. Each is resolvable but if the seam requires touching review.js in ways beyond composition the RED-first story changes.
findings.evidence:
§2 Tests bullet: 'review-runner.test.sh (NEW packet cases: a stub buildReviewPacket sees the composed list ...)' and 'resolve-review-loop.test.sh (... valid list echoed sorted/deduped ...)'. §1.2: JS resolver fails with 'review_packet_deny_extra[i] invalid pattern:

' while normalizeDenyList throws 'invalid deny-list pattern'. §2: shell 'emitted as a JSON array' with no ordering rule.
findings.evidence_reference: plan §1.2 message forms; §2 Tests bullet; §2 scripts/resolve-review-loop.sh bullet
findings.repair: Spike before sealing: confirm dispatchReview already accepts a deps or builder override usable from the test (else state the seam to add inside review.js); validate elements one at a time (normalizeDenyList([p])) to attribute the index and pattern; decide whether the shell emits config order (with normalization left to the builder) or sorted/deduped output, and write the resolver test against that decision.
